target_customer: Restaurant and cafe owners paying a cut of each pickup order; consumers ordering takeout
problem: Ordering and paying for takeout food required phone calls or waiting in line; local merchants lacked mobile ordering.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on pickup orders

founders.name: Jeffrey Byun
founders.background_notes: YC page says former bond trader.

founders.name: Ruddick Lawrence
founders.background_notes: Listed only as founder and CTO on the YC page.

competitors.name: Foodler
competitors.what: Online food ordering for delivery, expanded across the US in April 2011

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app plus merchant POS and payments integration; the hard part was self-serve merchant onboarding at scale.

defensibility.rationale: Merchant density in a city helped, but ordering apps were copyable by delivery platforms and chains.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Square bought the pickup business in late 2016 to complement Caviar.

market_need_then: Mobile restaurant ordering was growing in 2011 (GrubHub reported mobile at 20 percent of orders), and OrderAhead reported 200 merchants by August 2012 with about 100 signing in four weeks.

branding.domain_note: orderahead.com was the product domain; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name, press mostly about funding and the acquisition, and Order Ahead is a common phrase used by many restaurants.

outcome_analysis: OrderAhead launched pickup ordering in Palo Alto in 2012 after YC, raised 2.3 million dollars of seed in August 2012 and about 8 million of Series A in December 2013 at an estimated 30 million dollar valuation, and expanded to several large cities. Square bought only the pickup business in late 2016 for Caviar at an undisclosed price, which suggests an asset sale after delivery players and others crowded the category.
notes: The listed website is a Crunchbase page, so no company site was fetched. YC page says founded 2012 for a W11 company. Series A of about 8 million in December 2013 is from an aggregator and Bloomberg citing PitchBook (valuation 30 million, estimated); Wikipedia total funding 10.5 million. Square acquisition date is late 2016 per Wikipedia, reported March 2017 by Bloomberg; VentureBeat says only the pickup business was purchased. GrubHub source is dated after the batch; competitor present in 2011 per the same article. GrubHub Seamless (mobile orders 20 percent in 2011) was dropped from the competitor list because its source is dated 2013 or later.
